content_html:
Neuroscience ↔ AI

Neuroscience provides mechanisms (receptive fields, dopamine signals, predictive coding) that inspire AI architectures (CNNs, RL, generative models), while trained AI systems feed back into neuroscience by offering testable hypotheses and alignment tools (RSA) and by developing representations (e.g., grid-like codes) that mirror neural systems. Together they co-evolve shared solutions to representation, generalization, consolidation, and prediction.

Neuroscience → AI: Receptive fields inspired CNNs; attention & working memory informed Transformers; reward prediction signals shaped RL.
AI → Neuroscience: Goal-driven models mirror cortical representations; navigation agents develop grid-like codes; model–brain alignment tools (RSA) test hypotheses.
Shared themes: representation, generalization, memory consolidation, prediction, and control.
